question.text: Which one of the following statements is FALSE for hydrophilic sols?

options.text: These sols are reversible in nature.
Their viscosity is of the order of that of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></math>.
The sols cannot be easily coagulated.
They do not require electrolytes for stability.

solution.text:
Viscosity of hydrophilic sol >viscosity of H2O

Hydrophilic sol is more stable so can't be easily coagulated

Hydrophilic sols are reversible sols.

No electrolytes are required to stabilise hydrophilic sol.
